notes: Box score from the Bulls' 137–107 road win over the Brooklyn Nets on Nov 18, 2026, from the Covers box score, checked line by line against the Sports Illustrated box score, with game details from the Associated Press (via The Daily Gazette), the Chicago Sun-Times, Roundtable Sports (via Yahoo Sports), On Tap Sports Net and WJOX. All 137 Chicago points and all 107 Brooklyn points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores (37–39–35–26 to 21–30–26–30) add up to both totals: 76–51 Chicago at the half (AP; On Tap). Team totals (points in the paint 62–46, rebounds 46–29, assists 36–25, threes made 21–15, free throws made 10–14) and both biggest leads (Chicago 37, Brooklyn 2) are from the Covers box score; Chicago's 62 paint points and 46–29 rebounding edge match WJOX, and the 37-point lead matches the AP and the Sun-Times. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Wednesday's games.

Chicago's 137 points were its most this season (AP). The Bulls made a franchise-record 15 threes in the first half (AP; On Tap) and 21 in the game. Eight Bulls scored in double figures, and Matas Buzelis' 25 was a season high (AP). Brooklyn's only lead was 2–0 (AP). Nic Claxton, who spent seven seasons with the Nets, received a tribute video in the first quarter (Sun-Times). Chicago won for the third time in four games and for the first time in Brooklyn since Nov. 1, 2022 (AP). The Bulls host Washington on Friday, Nov 20 at 7 p.m. CT (8:00 PM ET; On Tap), and Washington won the first meeting 124–120 in Chicago on Oct. 24 (On Tap; Covers' schedule).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Patrick Williams' driving layup with 5.1 seconds left in the first quarter that made it 37–21 (On Tap). Chicago led 24–21 when Julius Randle scored with 3:00 left and then scored the last 13 points of the quarter (AP; On Tap; Roundtable Sports: over the final 2:46); the SI play-by-play lists Claxton's hook, threes by Isaac Okoro, Zach Collins and Norman Powell, then Williams' layup, so the board shows Bulls +14 to +16. It is drawn as a basket on a drive from the right of the lane; the recaps don't describe the finish beyond a driving layup. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Chicago Bulls or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Patrick Williams' listed 6-foot-6 and 235 pounds with No. 44 (RealGM), with his arms scaled to a reported 7-foot wingspan (Sportskeeda). He is drawn in Chicago's road colors with the default figure look (no approved look yet). It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
